questions.question:
You and your friend were playing together at your house on the same LAN. Your friend joined your game at: 192.168.1.10:7777

Then your friend goes home to a different network. Their home also uses 192.168.1.x private addresses.

They try the same address again: 192.168.1.10:7777

What happens?
answers: The packet travels across the Internet back to your PC
Their PC looks for 192.168.1.10 on their own local network
Their router converts it to your router's public address
Unity automatically redirects it through Relay

questions.question: You're hosting a game at home. A friend tries to join using your public IP and game port. Their request reaches your router but is not forwarded to your PC. What is the router missing?
answers: The identity of the player trying to join
The name of the Unity project running the game
The private LAN address of your friend's PC
A rule directing that game traffic to your PC

questions.question: Your internet works: your PC can connect to other computers and receive replies. What lets those replies get back to your PC?
answers: The router remembers the connection your PC started
The router sends the replies to every PC on your LAN
The other computer supplies your PC's private LAN address
The router finds a PC running the same application

questions.question: Your router forwards incoming game traffic to your desktop. You move the game host to your laptop but leave that rule unchanged. Where does the rule still send the traffic?
answers: To your laptop
To your friend's PC
To your desktop
To every PC on your LAN

questions.question: Port forwarding lets friends join the game you host at home. Why might you still choose Relay for a game that other players will host?
answers: Relay guarantees less latency than a direct connection
Relay takes over running the game from the host
Some players cannot access or configure their network's router
Relay gives every host PC a public IP address

questions.question: You host a game using Relay, with no port-forwarding rule. Your PC first establishes a connection to the Relay server. Later, Relay sends traffic from your friend back toward your PC. Why can that traffic get through your router?
answers: Relay installs a forwarding rule on your router
Your router remembers your PC's connection to Relay and lets traffic back through
The join code disables your router's incoming filter
Relay makes your host's private address publicly routable

questions.question: You're hosting the class game through Relay. A friend requests a pickup. Who decides whether the pickup succeeds?
answers: The Relay service forwarding the request
The friend's game sending the request
Whichever client owns the pickup object
Your host running the game server

questions.question:
You give your friend the Relay join code for your game. They enter it to join.

What does the join code help their game do?
answers: Find the Relay connection information for your game
Decode your public IP address and game port
Install a forwarding rule on your home router
Ask matchmaking to choose an available host
